Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY)
India's National Health Insurance Scheme, Explained Simply
A Public Awareness Reference Guide
1. Overview
Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) is a health insurance scheme run by the Government of India. Its purpose is to help poor and vulnerable families get hospital treatment without worrying about the cost. The scheme was launched in September 2018 and is managed by the National Health Authority (NHA), under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
PM-JAY gives eligible families cashless and paperless treatment at government and private hospitals that are registered, or "empanelled", under the scheme. This means a family does not need to pay money upfront or later claim reimbursement; the hospital is paid directly by the scheme. PM-JAY is described as one of the largest government-funded health insurance schemes in the world, and it works alongside Health and Wellness Centres, which provide routine and preventive care closer to home.
2. Eligibility
PM-JAY does not require families to pay a premium. Eligibility is largely based on the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC 2011) data, which identifies deprived rural and urban households. Broadly, a family may be eligible if it fits into certain deprivation categories, such as:
Rural households living in a kutcha (temporary or poorly built) house with only one room, or with no adult family member between 16 and 59 years of age.
Households headed by a woman with no adult male member in the family, or families with a disabled member and no able-bodied adult.
Families that depend mainly on manual casual labour, or belong to specific marginalised or landless categories identified in the SECC data.
In urban areas, eligibility is generally linked to specific occupational categories, such as street vendors, rag pickers, domestic workers, construction workers, and similar informal-sector occupations identified under the scheme.
In a more recent expansion, all senior citizens aged 70 years and above have been made eligible for PM-JAY coverage, regardless of their family's income, under a separate Ayushman Vay Vandana Card. Senior citizens who already have coverage under schemes like CGHS or ECHS can choose to continue with their existing scheme or switch to PM-JAY, but cannot use both at the same time.
Because eligibility is based on official databases and criteria that can be updated, families should not assume they are covered or excluded without checking. The scheme has its own online tool to confirm this individually.
3. Benefits
PM-JAY offers a defined package of benefits designed to reduce the financial burden of hospital treatment:
Health cover of up to five lakh rupees per family, per year, for hospital treatment. This amount is meant to be used as needed and is not divided per person; the whole family can draw from the same cover.
No restriction on family size, age, or gender; every member of an eligible family can be covered under one entitlement.
Coverage for pre-existing illnesses from the very first day, unlike many private insurance policies that apply a waiting period.
Cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals anywhere in the country, not just in the beneficiary's home state, which is useful for migrant workers and families who travel.
Coverage for a wide range of medical and surgical procedures, including common surgeries, cancer treatment, dialysis for kidney patients, newborn and child care, and many other secondary and tertiary care services.
Related expenses such as consultation, diagnostic tests, and medicines are generally covered for a short period before hospitalisation and after discharge, in addition to the hospital stay itself.
The exact list of covered procedures, package rates, and any recent additions are decided and periodically updated by the National Health Authority, so it is best to confirm current details for a specific treatment directly with an empanelled hospital or the official portal.
4. How to Apply
Step 1: Check Eligibility
Eligibility can be checked online through the official PM-JAY beneficiary portal or the Ayushman App, using a registered mobile number. After verifying the number with an OTP, the applicant selects their state and district and searches using details such as Aadhaar number, ration card number, or household ID to see if the family appears in the beneficiary list.
Step 2: Complete e-KYC and Get the Ayushman Card
If the family is listed as eligible, the applicant can proceed to complete e-KYC (identity verification) using Aadhaar, through OTP or biometric verification.
Once e-KYC is completed, the Ayushman card can be generated and downloaded online, or printed with help from a nearby Common Service Centre (CSC), empanelled hospital, or Ayushman Mitra.
Families without internet access can visit their nearest Common Service Centre, empanelled government hospital, or local health facility for assistance with checking eligibility and completing the process.
Step 3: Use the Card for Treatment
When hospital treatment is needed, the beneficiary can visit any empanelled hospital, show the Ayushman card along with identity proof, and receive treatment on a cashless basis for covered procedures. Hospital staff or an Ayushman Mitra posted at the hospital usually assist with verification and paperwork at this stage.
Because processes and portals are updated from time to time, it is advisable to keep Aadhaar, ration card, and other identity documents ready, and to confirm the latest application steps on the official website before applying.
5. Source Basis
This document is based on general, publicly available information about the Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY scheme, as described by the National Health Authority and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. No specific figures, dates, or claims that could not be reasonably confirmed have been included; all content has been rewritten in simple language and should be verified against the official scheme website for the latest details.
National Health Authority (NHA), Government of India — Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY — www.pmjay.gov.in
NHA Beneficiary Portal — beneficiary.nha.gov.in
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India (MoHFW) — www.mohfw.gov.in
National Health Mission (NHM), Government of India — www.nhm.gov.in
This content is for general awareness only. Please verify current details on the official scheme website before applying.
